text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: PD-INC-5128 — elevated 5xx for /v1/generate (canary traffic 10%)

pagerduty: Pager fired to @ashley-sre (on-call) and escalation policy observers. Trigger: 5xx rate > 8% over 2m for route /v1/generate.

ashley-sre: acked. I'm looking. any idea what the canary release id is?

deploy-bot: canary release: canary-2026-03-14-09f4 (traffic split: 10% to canary, 90% stable).

ben-eng: seeing p95 latency jump +2.4s and 5xx ratio climbed to ~22% in the canary cluster. Logs show kv-cache eviction errors immediately after startup. snippet:```
ERROR kvcache: eviction failure: lease not found
WARN model: failed to allocate transient cache slot
```

carol-sre: that matches an instrumented kernel path we rolled in q2 quant changes. could be regression in the kernel selection for small batch sizes.

ashley-sre: ok plan: 1) pause canary traffic, 2) promote quick rollback if pause doesn't stabilize, 3) notify customers if needed.

ashley-sre: pausing canary routing now -> `redwood route update /v1/generate --traffic-canary 0`

deploy-bot: traffic update submitted, canary traffic set to 0%. propagation expected <30s.

ben-eng: metrics dropping but still seeing tail errors on a few hosts. might be some warmed nodes still serving older kernels — checking autoscaler and node pool.

carol-sre: if we can't stabilize in 5m we should rollback the canary image entirely. safer than partial fixes.

jordan-prodops: what is customer impact? any paid tenants hit? support queue?

ashley-sre: initial telemetry shows spike for a subset of customers on hosted-api who hit /v1/generate with long contexts — p95 for those tenants up from 1s to 6s and increased error surface. no major enterprise SLA breach yet but warnings.

ben-eng: cross-checking request ids... some requests hit v2-quant kernels. I can force a rollback to stable image `stable-2026-03-08` if needed.

ashley-sre: do it. runbook rollback command:```
# rollback canary image on runtime pool
redwood deploy rollback --service=inference-runtime --from=canary-2026-03-14-09f4 --to=stable-2026-03-08 --force
```

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by ben-eng. starting hooks. estimated 2m to apply to all canary nodes.

pagerduty: Note: initial pager escalations to observers suspended for acknowledged pages.

ashley-sre: I'm escalating to sec-ops to confirm if any auth/token issues observed while we rollback (just in case). @carol-sre please lead the post-rollback verification.

carol-sre: will do. verification checklist: 1) p95 < 800ms for /v1/generate across released pools, 2) 5xx rate <1% sustained for 5m, 3) CPU/GPU memory normal, 4) no new kvcache evictions in logs.

ben-eng: rollback completed on runtime nodes at 1777009180. reverting autoscaler config to pre-canary values.

deploy-bot: rollback hooks finished. health checks passing on 12/12 hosts.

ashley-sre: metrics look good. p95 back to ~450ms, 5xx ~0.6%. closing the active page in PD.

pagerduty: Page resolved by ashley-sre at 1777009252. Incident ticket PD-INC-5128 transitioned to "resolved (rollback)".

jordan-prodops: flagging for customer comms: small set of hosted users saw degraded perf for ~6m. recommend one-sentence note in status page and direct DM to any customers who filed tickets.

ashley-sre: agree. I'll draft status and send to comms. Also scheduling a quick postmortem sync at +30m to determine root cause and action items.

carol-sre: action items preliminary: 1) revert kernel selection change for small-batch quant path, 2) add guard in runtime: fail closed on kvcache init error, 3) add canary warmup probes to traffic ramp scripts.

ben-eng: logging extra correlation ids and adding a short-lived feature-flag to gate the quant path while we test.

ashley-sre: handing incident to carol-sre for followup and postmortem. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

carol-sre: acknowledged handoff. I'll own the incident writeup and timeline. leaving this thread open until postmortem published.

incident-bot: incident thread closed for active paging but thread will remain for post-incident notes.
